prior_importants.description: A status cell that is not exactly `verbatim`, `adapted` or `local only` (for example `Verbatim`) skips the deviation check and the verbatim check. The script still exits 0.

findings.description: The row-coverage loop lists files with `find "$SKILLS_DIR" -type f`, so untracked or git-ignored files such as a Finder `.DS_Store` or a vim swap file under `.claude/skills/` make the script print `FAIL: <x>/.DS_Store has no row` and exit 1 on a clean tree. List tracked files only, with `git ls-files -- "$SKILLS_DIR"`.

Nothing checks up front that the pinned commit exists in the upstream checkout. With a shallow clone (`git clone --depth 1`) or a wrong directory, every non-local row fails with `<path> is not upstream at the pin`, which blames each path rather than the checkout. One check before the loop fixes it: `git -C "$up" cat-file -e "$pin^{commit}"`, exiting with a clear message when it fails.

An `adapted` row whose local file now equals upstream at the pin still passes, printing `0 changed lines`. The ledger defines adapted as "differs", so its deviation bullets go stale unnoticed. In the else branch, add `[ "$changed" -gt 0 ] || bad "$rel is adapted but equals upstream"`.
